entities.name: Scrub Typhus
entities.description: Acute life-threatening zoonotic febrile illness caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and transmitted by larval trombiculid mites (chiggers), characterized by disseminated endothelial microvascular infection, perivascular cuffing vasculitis, and potential multiorgan failure.

entities.name: Leptotrombidium Mite Larva Chigger Bite
entities.description: Painless bite from the microscopic six-legged larval stage of trombiculid mites (chiggers), predominantly Leptotrombidium deliense, L. akamushi, and L. fletcheri, which feed on liquefied host epidermal tissue.

entities.name: Scrub Vegetation & Agricultural Terrain Exposure
entities.description: Occupational or recreational exposure to overgrown secondary scrub vegetation, grasslands, forest fringes, riverbanks, or rice fields ('scrub typhus islands') during weeding, harvesting, or monsoon periods.

entities.name: Tsutsugamushi Triangle Endemic Residence or Travel
entities.description: Residence in or travel to the endemic Asia-Pacific Tsutsugamushi Triangle spanning South, Southeast, and East Asia to Northern Australia, as well as emerging focal areas in South America (Chile) and Africa.

entities.name: Orientia tsutsugamushi
entities.description: Obligate intracellular Gram-negative alphaproteobacterium that selectively infects microvascular endothelial cells and monocyte-macrophages, inducing disseminated microvascular leakage and systemic inflammation.

entities.name: Cigarette-Burn Cutaneous Necrotic Eschar in Flexural Folds
entities.description: Pathognomonic primary cutaneous lesion beginning as an indolent erythematous macule/papule that ulcerates into a black necrotic crust with an erythematous halo resembling a cigarette burn, primarily in warm, moist, intertriginous skin folds (groin, axilla, perineum, sub-mammary creases, waistline).

entities.name: Regional Tender Lymphadenopathy Draining Eschar
entities.description: Painful, tender enlargement of localized lymph node basins draining the cutaneous eschar site appearing early in the illness course and preceding generalized lymphadenopathy.

entities.name: Acute Sensorineural Hearing Loss and Tinnitus
entities.description: Sudden-onset subjective hearing impairment, tinnitus, or bilateral sensory deafness occurring in 20–35% of patients during acute infection due to cranial nerve VIII or cochlear microvasculitis.

entities.name: Bilateral Non-Purulent Bulbar Conjunctival Suffusion
entities.description: Prominent bilateral bulbar conjunctival hyperemia and injection without purulent discharge or exudate, frequently accompanied by subconjunctival hemorrhages and photophobia.

entities.name: Centrifugal Trunk-to-Extremity Maculopapular Exanthem
entities.description: Transient non-pruritic erythematous maculopapular eruption appearing on the trunk around days 4 to 6 of fever, spreading centrifugally to proximal extremities and fading over several days.

entities.name: Normal WBC with Prominent Bandemia and Moderate Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Admission complete blood count pattern showing normal or mild leukocyte counts (8,000–14,000/µL) with prominent toxic left shift (bandemia >10%) and moderate thrombocytopenia (platelets 50,000–100,000/µL).

entities.name: Marked CRP Elevation with Disproportionate Transaminitis
entities.description: Substantially elevated acute-phase C-reactive protein (CRP > 50–100 mg/L) paired with 2–5x ULN elevation of AST and ALT transaminases and mild alkaline phosphatase elevation reflecting acute endothelial and hepatic injury.

entities.name: Bilateral Reticulonodular Interstitial Infiltrates on Triage Chest Radiograph
entities.description: Triage plain chest radiograph showing prominent bronchovascular markings, Kerley B lines, bilateral reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates, and small reactive pleural effusions consistent with interstitial pneumonitis.

entities.name: Mild-to-Moderate Hepatosplenomegaly on Bedside Ultrasound
entities.description: Point-of-care abdominal ultrasound demonstrating diffuse homogeneous splenomegaly and hepatomegaly in the absence of focal liver abscesses, intrahepatic biliary dilatation, or gallbladder wall edema.

entities.name: Failure to Defervesce Within 48 to 72 Hours of Doxycycline Therapy
entities.description: Persistence of high fever and clinical failure despite 48 to 72 hours of appropriate oral or intravenous doxycycline or azithromycin therapy strongly excludes uncomplicated scrub typhus.

entities.name: Purulent Exudative Skin Ulcer or Fluctuant Subcutaneous Abscess
entities.description: Presence of purulent drainage, frank exudate, or fluctuant subcutaneous abscess formation at a cutaneous lesion site rules out the characteristically dry, indolent, non-purulent necrotic eschar of scrub typhus.

entities.name: Severe Leukocytosis Exceeding 20,000/µL Without Secondary Infection
entities.description: Marked leukocytosis (>20,000/µL) at admission in the absence of concurrent pyogenic bacterial superinfection strongly argues against uncomplicated scrub typhus.

entities.name: Normal C-Reactive Protein Under 10 mg/L in Sustained High Fever
entities.description: Normal or near-normal C-reactive protein level (<10 mg/L) in a patient with sustained high remittent fever strongly rules out scrub typhus, which uniformly triggers intense endothelial inflammation with CRP > 50 mg/L.

entities.name: Dengue
entities.description: Arboviral illness presenting with acute high fever, severe retro-orbital pain, arthralgia, and early critical-phase plasma leakage.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal infection transmitted via freshwater/urine contact presenting with high fever, conjunctival suffusion, severe calf pain, and jaundice.

entities.name: Malaria
entities.description: Mosquito-borne intraerythrocytic parasitic infection presenting with paroxysmal fevers, rigors, hemolytic anemia, and splenomegaly.

entities.name: Murine Typhus
entities.description: Flea-borne rickettsiosis caused by Rickettsia typhi endemic to urban, suburban, and port environments associated with rodents.

entities.name: Rapid Defervescence Within 48 Hours of Doxycycline Therapy
entities.description: Complete temperature normalization and symptomatic relief within 24 to 48 hours of starting oral or IV Doxycycline (100 mg twice daily), serving as a diagnostic therapeutic confirmation hallmark.

entities.name: Clinical Defervescence with Oral Azithromycin Therapy
entities.description: Rapid clinical cure and fever clearance following oral Azithromycin (500 mg once daily for 3–5 days), serving as the first-line therapeutic regimen for pregnant patients, children, and doxycycline-tolerant geographic strains.

entities.name: Intrinsic Resistance to Beta-Lactams Aminoglycosides and Fluoroquinolones
entities.description: Orientia tsutsugamushi possesses total intrinsic resistance to penicillins, cephalosporins (e.g. ceftriaxone), carbapenems, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones; empirical administration leads to therapeutic failure and progressive clinical deterioration.

relationships.target: Leptotrombidium Mite Larva Chigger Bite
relationships.keywords: TRANSMITTED_BY, vector transmission, trombiculid mite, chigger bite
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Scrub Typhus is transmitted exclusively through the bite of the microscopic six-legged larva of trombiculid mites (chiggers), predominantly Leptotrombidium deliense, L. akamushi, and L. fletcheri, during extracellular host tissue feeding.

relationships.target: Scrub Vegetation & Agricultural Terrain Exposure
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, agricultural hazard, occupational exposure
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Acquisition occurs following outdoor occupational or recreational exposure to neglected scrub vegetation, secondary grasslands, forest fringes, riverbanks, or rice fields ('scrub typhus islands') during weeding, harvesting, or monsoon periods.

relationships.target: Tsutsugamushi Triangle Endemic Residence or Travel
relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, geographic endemicity, travel history, Tsutsugamushi Triangle
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Endemic to the expansive Tsutsugamushi Triangle covering South Asia, Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Northern Australia, with emerging documented foci in South America (Chile) and Africa.

relationships.target: Orientia tsutsugamushi
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGEN, causative agent, microbiology, obligate intracellular
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Scrub Typhus is caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi, an obligate intracellular Gram-negative alphaproteobacterium that selectively invades vascular endothelial cells, triggering disseminated vasculitis and perivascular cuffing.

relationships.target: Cigarette-Burn Cutaneous Necrotic Eschar in Flexural Folds
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, cutaneous eschar
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] The pathognomonic cutaneous eschar is a painless, non-pruritic black necrotic crust with an indurated erythematous halo resembling a cigarette burn, identified in 50–90% of patients upon thorough search of warm, moist flexural areas (groin, axilla, perineum, sub-mammary folds, waistline).

relationships.target: Regional Tender Lymphadenopathy Draining Eschar
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, cardinal sign, localized adenopathy, lymphatic drainage
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Marked enlargement and tenderness of the regional lymph nodes draining the anatomical site of the eschar is present in the acute phase, preceding generalized lymphadenopathy.

relationships.target: Acute Sensorineural Hearing Loss and Tinnitus
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, sensory hallmark, cranial neuropathy, cochlear vasculitis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Acute sensorineural hearing impairment, tinnitus, or subjective deafness occurs in 20–35% of patients during acute febrile illness secondary to cranial nerve VIII or cochlear microvasculitis, serving as a highly specific diagnostic indicator.

relationships.target: Bilateral Non-Purulent Bulbar Conjunctival Suffusion
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, ocular hallmark, conjunctival suffusion, microvascular injection
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Striking bilateral bulbar conjunctival hyperemia and suffusion without purulent discharge or exudate occurs during the acute febrile phase due to ocular microvascular endothelial involvement.

relationships.target: Centrifugal Trunk-to-Extremity Maculopapular Exanthem
relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, exanthem, maculopapular rash, systemic vasculitis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] A transient, erythematous, non-pruritic maculopapular rash appears over the trunk around illness days 4 to 6, spreading centrifugally to the proximal extremities and fading over several days.

relationships.target: Normal WBC with Prominent Bandemia and Moderate Thrombocytopenia
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, CBC, left shift, thrombocytopenia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission complete blood count typically demonstrates a normal or mildly elevated white blood cell count (8,000–14,000/µL) paired with prominent toxic left shift (bandemia >10%) and moderate thrombocytopenia (platelets 50,000–100,000/µL).

relationships.target: Marked CRP Elevation with Disproportionate Transaminitis
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, inflammatory markers, LFT, CRP
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Marked elevation of C-reactive protein (CRP > 50–100 mg/L) paired with moderate AST and ALT transaminitis (2–5x upper limit of normal) reflects acute systemic endothelial injury and distinguishes scrub typhus from common viral infections.

relationships.target: Bilateral Reticulonodular Interstitial Infiltrates on Triage Chest Radiograph
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission imaging, chest radiograph, interstitial pneumonitis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Plain chest radiography at admission reveals bilateral reticulonodular interstitial opacities, prominent bronchovascular markings, Kerley B lines, and mild reactive pleural effusions consistent with rickettsial interstitial pneumonitis.

relationships.target: Mild-to-Moderate Hepatosplenomegaly on Bedside Ultrasound
relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission imaging, POCUS ultrasound, organomegaly
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside ultrasound demonstrates homogeneous splenomegaly and hepatomegaly without focal hepatic abscesses, biliary tract dilation, or prominent gallbladder wall thickening.

relationships.target: Failure to Defervesce Within 48 to 72 Hours of Doxycycline Therapy
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, treatment failure
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Failure of a febrile patient to show clinical defervescence and symptomatic improvement within 48 to 72 hours of appropriate oral or IV doxycycline therapy strongly rules out uncomplicated scrub typhus and necessitates immediate alternate evaluation.

relationships.target: Purulent Exudative Skin Ulcer or Fluctuant Subcutaneous Abscess
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, lesion morphology
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of purulent, fluctuant, or grossly suppurative skin ulcers rules out the characteristically dry, indolent, non-purulent cigarette-burn necrotic eschar of scrub typhus.

relationships.target: Severe Leukocytosis Exceeding 20,000/µL Without Secondary Infection
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, CBC cutoff
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Severe leukocytosis (WBC > 20,000/µL) at admission in the absence of documented bacterial superinfection strongly argues against scrub typhus, which characteristically presents with normal or mildly elevated leukocytes.

relationships.target: Normal C-Reactive Protein Under 10 mg/L in Sustained High Fever
relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, normal inflammatory markers
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] A normal or near-normal C-reactive protein (<10 mg/L) in a patient presenting with sustained high fever (>39°C) and acute illness strongly excludes scrub typhus, which reliably induces intense systemic inflammation with CRP > 50 mg/L.

relationships.target: Dengue
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, dengue
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Dengue presents with profound leukopenia (WBC < 4,000/µL), critical hemoconcentration (hematocrit rise >= 20%), gallbladder wall thickening, and plasma leakage at defervescence; Dengue NEVER presents with a necrotic cigarette-burn eschar, acute sensorineural deafness, prominent localized lymphadenopathy, or high CRP (> 50 mg/L).

relationships.target: Leptospirosis
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, leptospirosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leptospirosis features marked neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC > 15,000/µL), severe gastrocnemius calf tenderness, deep conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and oliguric acute renal failure following freshwater immersion; Leptospirosis does NOT cause a cigarette-burn cutaneous eschar or acute sensorineural hearing loss.

relationships.target: Malaria
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, malaria
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Malaria is characterized by periodic teeth-chattering rigors, marked hemolytic anemia (unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, elevated LDH, low haptoglobin), and blood smears positive for intraerythrocytic Plasmodium parasites; Malaria lacks an eschar, regional lymphadenopathy, and sensorineural deafness.

relationships.target: Murine Typhus
relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, murine typhus
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Murine typhus (Rickettsia typhi) is transmitted by rat fleas in urban port environments rather than chiggers in rural scrub vegetation, exceptionally rarely produces an eschar (<1%), and does not cause acute sensorineural hearing loss.

relationships.target: Rapid Defervescence Within 48 Hours of Doxycycline Therapy
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, therapeutic verification, doxycycline, diagnostic therapeutic trial
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Administration of oral or intravenous Doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) results in rapid defervescence, reduction of severe headache, and hemodynamic stabilization within 24 to 48 hours, acting as a diagnostic therapeutic hallmark.

relationships.target: Clinical Defervescence with Oral Azithromycin Therapy
relationships.keywords: RESPONDS_TO, therapeutic verification, azithromycin, macrolide therapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Administration of oral Azithromycin (500 mg once daily for 3–5 days) achieves rapid fever clearance and cure rates equivalent to doxycycline, serving as the first-line therapeutic regimen for pregnant patients, children, and regions with doxycycline-tolerant strains.

relationships.target: Intrinsic Resistance to Beta-Lactams Aminoglycosides and Fluoroquinolones
relationships.keywords: INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO, antibiotic failure, intrinsic resistance, beta-lactam
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Orientia tsutsugamushi is naturally intrinsically resistant to all beta-lactams (penicillins, cephalosporins including ceftriaxone, carbapenems), aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin); empirical treatment with these agents results in persistent fever, multi-organ deterioration, and avoidable mortality.
